news.title: Top Flemish universities hike non-EU tuition fees
news.summary_en: Several Flemish universities have raised tuition fees for non-EU students in response to stricter federal funding rules, in the latest policy shift affecting Belgium’s international education sector.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Five things we learned about expanding UK schools into India at IPSEF 2026
news.summary_en: From “the long, very long game” of parental decision‑making to co‑branding with local giants, here are five takeaways on taking British K‑12 schools into India from this year’s IPSEF conference.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: “Competitor countries will be celebrating”: sector bodies slam Australia’s visa fee hike
news.summary_en: Sector bodies have reacted strongly to Australia’s latest visa fee increases, expressing disappointment and warning the changes risk weakening the country’s appeal as a global study destination.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Student visa fees rise again as Australia adds ELICOS pricing tier
news.summary_en: Australia has hiked visa fees overnight, lifting the student visa to AUD $2,500 and introducing a separate $2,050 ELICOS rate.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: UK universities to sponsor refugees under new asylum “safe routes” overhaul
news.summary_en: UK universities will be able to directly sponsor refugees to study in Britain under new government plans to expand “safe and legal routes” for those seeking protection.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: ETS acquires ACT in major US education assessment deal
news.summary_en: Global testing giant ETS has today acquired ACT, the organisation behind America's standardised college admissions test.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: The students we lose after admission: why payment plans matter more than ever
news.summary_en: As volatile currencies and international exchange shortages continue to disrupt student journeys, Bimpe Femi-Oyewo says payment plans will not just expand access to education but will give institutions a competitive advantage.
news.author: Bimpe Femi-Oyewo

news.title: IIT Bombay eyes 2027 launch for first overseas sub-campus in the US
news.summary_en: The Indian Institute of Technology Bombay is set to establish its first academic presence in the US through a partnership with the State University of New York (SUNY) at Old Westbury, with the first certificate courses expected to launch in 2027.
news.author: Abhishek Nair

news.title: US terminates protection status for Haitians and Syrians
news.summary_en: The US Supreme Court has granted authorisation to the Trump Administration to end Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti and Syria, putting hundreds of thousands of people at risk of deportation.
news.author: Polly Nash

news.title: Australia Bill proposes shift of international student allocation powers to ATEC
news.summary_en: Australia has introduced legislation that would shift the allocation of international student commencements to the Australian Tertiary Education Commission (ATEC), if passed.
news.author: Kim Martin

news.title: Everyone’s an expert in UKVI compliance now. Are the real experts getting a look‑in?
news.summary_en: The conversation about compliance is getting crowded, with the real expertise in danger of being drowned out. Mike Strong and Alex Lock consider the next steps for colleagues seeking to reclaim the conversation.
news.author: Alex Lock and Mike Strong

news.title: France strengthens push to become leading destination for global researchers
news.summary_en: France is looking to strengthen its position as a destination for international researchers, even as competition for global scientific talent intensifies and doctoral enrolments begin to decline.
news.author: Kim Martin
